question_text: Find the average rate of change of s = f(t) = 2t² + 3 between t = 2 and t = 4.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say whether you differentiate here, and what you divide by.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the average rate of change
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is an average rate of change question, not a derivative question. Write the difference quotient before any numbers go in. Both f(4) and f(2) are needed — one alone gives nothing.
steps.memory_tip: Average rate uses two points and a subtraction; instantaneous rate uses one point and a derivative.
lines: This is an average rate of change question. Over an interval the average rate is the
change in s divided by the change in t, so no differentiation is used here.

recall.must_convey: That the average rate of change is [f(4) − f(2)]/(4 − 2), a difference quotient and not a derivative.
accept: average rate is f of four minus f of two divided by four minus two
change in s divided by change in t over the interval
this one is not a derivative, it is a difference quotient
average rate ante f of four minus f of two by two
f of four is thirty five and f of two is eleven
heard_as: f of four minus f of two

steps.why: An average rate over an interval compares two end values, so it is a difference quotient. The derivative would give the rate at one instant, which is a different question.
common_mistakes: Differentiating and giving f′(t) = 4t, which is the instantaneous rate and not the average rate.
Using only f(4) and forgetting to subtract f(2).

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 24/2 = 12. Divide by 4 − 2 = 2, not by 4. The stem gives no units for s and t, so the answer is written as units of s per unit of t.
steps.memory_tip: Change in s over change in t — the same shape as the slope of the line joining the two points on the graph.

lines.text: ∴ average rate of change = 12 units of s per unit of t

accept: thirty five minus eleven is twenty four, divided by two is twelve
the average rate of change is twelve
divide the change in s by the change in t to get twelve
twenty four by two, twelve vasthundi

steps.why: The answer can be checked against the derivative: f′(t) = 4t gives 8 at t = 2 and 16 at t = 4, and 12 lies between them, as an average rate over the interval must.
common_mistakes: Writing 12t, as if the answer were still a function of t.
Giving 24, the change in s, as the rate.
Quoting f′(3) = 12 as the method — the number agrees here only because f is a quadratic, and it would not for other functions.
